# Klaudia Burton

# Directory of Equity and Social Justice

![](/media/uploads/2026/10/klaudia-burton.jpg)

- She said, “For a lot of our students, this is their space,” she continued, “This is their space where they come out to us and they don’t for their families, some of them don’t have that opportunity. And that’s really unfortunate, but we want to make sure that they are seen and heard and valued.”
- Burton also said the district has a form students complete to identify their preferred names and who the information could be used with saying, “If I have a conference with a family member, am I allowed to use that [name],” she said, referencing the form.

Regarding President Trump’s directives to get rid of race-based diversity, equity, and inclusion practices in schools, [Burton said](https://web.archive.org/web/20260221094519/https:/eastlansingportrait.com/4502/opinion/dont-deny-dei/): “There is a lot of obeying in advance. There’s only the threat of [losing funding because of keeping DEI]. I have a duty and responsibility here. There’s absolutely nothing I’m changing.”

On the topic of adding the Persian Nowruz holiday (a holiday that celebrates the arrival of spring) to the school calendar [Burton said](https://web.archive.org/web/20240911044131/https:/news.jrn.msu.edu/2023/11/east-lansing-public-schools-holiday-calendar-updated-to-include-persian-nowruz/), “Our calendars often focus on Christian dominance, so it is important for us to recognize our rich diversity within our community,” said Burton. “That’s why we made this calendar to ensure that we are attentive to the differences within our community and that we’re serving our students and families who partake in these cultural and religious observations.”

Burton claimed student dress codes targeted women and people of color.

- “We know that a lot of dress code policies inherently target women, but also students of color  -  particularly Black females. Rules on hats, hoodies and sagging jeans also target a lot of cultural normatives,” [said Klaudia Burton](https://web.archive.org/web/20260917145433/https:/lansingcitypulse.com/is-your-school-dress-code-biased-against-girls-probably/), director of equity and social justice for East Lansing Schools. “It comes back to how society views women and the general sexualization of women’s bodies.”
